The row's two verses at byte tier: oshb:Prov.16.10, קֶ֤סֶם עַֽל שִׂפְתֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל פִּֽיו; oshb:Prov.16.11, פֶּ֤לֶס וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל אַבְנֵי כִֽיס. The auditor's byte facts all verify: בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט and מִ֭שְׁפָּט are distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (במשפט in 4 verses book-wide: Prov.16.10, 18.5, 24.23, 29.4; bare משפט in 12: Prov.2.8, 8.20, 12.5, 13.23, 16.8, 16.11, 17.23, 19.28, 21.7, 21.15, 28.5, 29.26), the seam Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11 shares no word-bound skeleton token, the bare form stands two verses earlier as מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Prov.16.8, and the 16:11 token re-sweeps at 1 verse byte tier and 13 accent-stripped including Prov.16.10. Second, the corpus does not apply a word-bound-only seam metric: the adjacent row spanning Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 rests on the royal noun across the word-bound-empty seam Prov.16.13|Prov.16.14 (מְ֭לָכִים plural against מֶ֥לֶךְ singular), the row spanning Prov.18.18-Prov.18.19 rests on a bare form against a waw-prefixed qere, and the row spanning Prov.15.31-Prov.15.33 links מ֭וּסָר to מוּסַ֣ר at skeleton tier only; the rows spanning Prov.16.1 and Prov.16.9 refused the 16:1-16:9 envelope because the only recurring token there is the divine name, which they discount as non-content (the bare word-bound token alone stands in 70 verses book-wide), plus three fully empty seams - a different test from the one this row faces. Third, the mishpat object is more distinctive than either the row or the finding states: the contiguous-skeleton sweep returns 20 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel, verse count) with exactly two adjacent pairs, Prov.2.8|Prov.2.9 in the lectures and Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11, so within the Solomon collection Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16 this seam is the sole adjacent recurrence of the lexeme among its 12 verses there; and the owner-ruled strategy itself names a kings run at 16:10-15 as a cluster candidate, so it contemplates 16:10 and 16:11 inside a multi-verse unit. The cluster therefore has byte-grounded cohesion named in its rationale, which is what the collection's granularity law requires, and the filed high (a load-bearing defect: a cluster with no byte cohesion) is not supported. What is defective, and medium: the rationale presents the object as 'the shared noun' with only a within-span digit ('sweep: 2 consecutive verses'), never states that the two forms are distinct word-bound tokens, names no tier, and omits the book-wide and collection digits that actually distinguish the pair; and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects only the forward extension and never states or rejects the collection's default single_proverb atomization, the mandated rival for every proverb_cluster row. Downgrade to medium. Both sides of every seam the proposal touches, at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.16.9, לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.16.10; the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.16.12, תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא, shares none with oshb:Prov.16.11 (the verb עֲשׂ֣וֹת and the noun מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ are different lexemes of one root); the interior seam carries the mishpat lexeme. The governing rule is the collection's catchword law, and by it the outer edges are empty either way while the interior seam is the one place in the collection where the lexeme recurs in adjacent verses. Span ruling: decline_proposal. Retiring the pair is not byte-compelled: it would dissolve a byte-true catchword on the strength of a word-bound-only metric the corpus applies nowhere else, and it would leave מֶ֑לֶךְ at oshb:Prov.16.10 as an unpaired royal-noun verse directly before the kings run, reopening the seam that the rows spanning Prov.16.10-Prov.16.11 and Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 currently argue coherently (each states from bytes why 16:11 carries no royal noun and why 16:10 is bound forward by mishpat). The auditor's alternative remedy is the byte-supported one and is endorsed as a field-repair proposal only: re-cut the rationale to name the object as one lexeme in prefixed and bare forms that are distinct word-bound tokens, carry the digits above (4 and 12 word-bound; 20 contiguous with two adjacent pairs book-wide, one in this collection), and state and reject the single_proverb atomization on those grounds.
